questions.text: What is the median of data if its mode is 15 and the mean is 30?
questions.solution:
Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median [latex]-[/latex] 2 Mean.

15 = 3M [latex]-[/latex] 60 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] M = 25

Answer: 25

questions.text:
The value of the integral given below is
[latex]\int_{0}^{\pi }x^{2}cosxdx[/latex]
questions.solution:
Integrate by parts: [latex]\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x[/latex]

From 0 to [latex]\pi[/latex]: [latex](0+2\pi(-1)-0)-0=-2\pi[/latex]

Answer: [latex]-2\pi[/latex]

questions.text:
With respect to the numerical evaluation of the definite integral,[latex]K=\int_{a}^{b}x^{2}dx[/latex] , where a and b are given, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
(I) The value of K obtained using the trapezoidal rule is always greater than or equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
(II) The value of K obtained using the Simpson's rule is always equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]x^2[/latex] is convex, so the chord (trapezoid) lies above the curve [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] trapezoidal value [latex]\ge[/latex] exact [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- II: Simpson's rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.

Answer: Both I and II
